questions.stem: A car rental desk asks the issuer to approve 400.00 when the customer picks up the car, and the final bill three days later comes to 260.00. The link accepts both 0100 and 0200. Which first message leaves the cardholder's account right during those three days?

options.text: An 0100, since its approval holds the 400.00 and the final 260.00 is what moves later
options.says: an approved 0100 places a hold; the money moves when the transaction is completed and cleared with the final amount

options.text: An 0100, since its approval moves the 400.00 at once and the extra 140.00 is refunded later
options.says: an approved 0100 moves no money; it only holds the amount

options.text: An 0200, since its approval holds the 400.00 until the final bill of 260.00 is sent
options.says: an approved 0200 posts the debit at once; it is not a hold

options.text: An 0200, since its approval moves the 400.00 at once and the final bill needs no message
options.says: posting 400.00 at once charges 140.00 too much until a second message gives it back

origin.section: 4.2. The Second Digit Says What an Approval Commits

questions.stem: An issuer's host was down for two minutes. Since it came back, it keeps receiving 0421 messages whose STANs it has no record of. What should it send back for each one?

options.text: An 0430, since the answer to a repeat is the answer to the message it repeats
options.says: the answer drops the repeat mark, so an 0421 is answered by an 0430, and the reversal it carries still has to be applied

options.text: An 0431, since the answer keeps the repeat digit of the message it answers
options.says: setResponseMTI turns an 0421 into an 0430; the answer is to the message, not to one attempt

options.text: Nothing at all, since a message with an unknown STAN cannot repeat anything it saw
options.says: the 0420 it repeats arrived during the outage; the repeat is the first the host sees of that reversal

options.text: Nothing at all, since the acquirer sends the 0420 again once the 0421 goes unanswered
options.says: the acquirer keeps sending 0421 repeats until it is acknowledged or gives up; it never goes back to 0420

origin.section: 4.3.1. Spot the Problem: The Dispatcher That Ignored a Repeat

questions.stem: An 0200 for 64.90 gets no answer within the acquirer's timeout, and the terminal has shown the cashier a failure. What does the acquirer send next?

options.text: The same 0200 again, since a second answer shows whether the first one was approved
options.says: if the first was approved, a second 0200 is a second purchase

options.text: The same 0200 with a new STAN, since the issuer then treats it as a fresh attempt
options.says: a fresh attempt is exactly the second purchase that charges the cardholder twice

options.text: An 0420 with a STAN of its own, since it undoes an approval and changes nothing otherwise
options.says: a reversal is a new message on the link; it gives the money back if the purchase was approved and is harmless if not

options.text: An 0420 with the purchase's STAN, since the issuer finds the purchase through field 11
options.says: the issuer finds the original through field 90; field 11 is the reversal's own number as a new message on the link

origin.section: 4.4. A Request Without an Answer Is Reversed, Never Sent Again

questions.stem: An acquirer's 0800 echo test gets no 0810 within its timeout, though the link otherwise looks healthy. What does the acquirer owe the host for that 0800?

options.text: A reversal of it, since the host may have acted on it before its answer was lost
options.says: an 0800 touches no account, so there is nothing to undo

options.text: A repeat of it as an 0801, since an unanswered message is repeated until acknowledged
options.says: repeats are for advices, which report something that happened; an echo reports nothing

options.text: Nothing for it, since it changes no account and the next one starts afresh
options.says: network management messages commit nothing, so an unanswered one needs no clean-up

options.text: Nothing for it, since the host sends its own 0810 once the link has been quiet a while
options.says: an 0810 answers an 0800; the host does not send one on its own

origin.section: 4.2. The Second Digit Says What an Approval Commits
